hint_en: Which one can be checked with historical records? Which uses the value word 'fairest'?
hint_zh: 邊句可以用歷史紀錄核實？邊句用咗「最公平」呢類價值字眼？
explain_en: A can be verified by facts, so it is positive. B is a value judgement about fairness, so it is normative.
explain_zh: A 可以用事實驗證，係 positive；B 係對公平與否嘅 value judgement，係 normative。

prompt_en: Grandpa chooses to keep drying salt ($120/month) instead of factory work ($180, plus $20 fares) or fishing ($150). His opportunity cost is:
prompt_zh: 阿爺揀繼續曬鹽（每月 $120），放棄工廠打工（$180，另加車費 $20）同打魚（$150），opportunity cost 係：
hint_en: Which two are given up? Even after fares, is the factory still highest?
hint_zh: 放棄咗邊兩樣？就算扣埋車費，工廠仲係咪最高？
explain_en: Only the highest-valued option forgone counts. Even net of fares, the factory ($160) beats fishing ($150).
explain_zh: 只計最高價值嘅放棄選項。就算扣埋車費，工廠淨值 $160 仍然高過打魚 $150。

prompt_en: Grandpa's father spent $3,000 building the salt pans in the 1940s. That money is a ____ cost and should not affect the decision.
prompt_zh: 阿爺嘅阿爸 1940 年代起鹽田用咗 $3,000，呢筆錢係 ① cost，唔應該影響決定。
options_zh: 歷史|金錢|時間|全部
hint_en: Can that money be recovered whatever he chooses today?
hint_zh: 嗰筆錢今日點揀都拎唔拎得返？
explain_en: Historical cost is not a cost.
explain_zh: Historical cost 唔係 cost。

prompt_en: If Grandpa chooses factory work instead, the full cost is:
prompt_zh: 如果阿爺改揀工廠打工，full cost 係：
hint_en: Money cost is the fare; non-money cost is the best alternative use of his time – which is?
hint_zh: Money cost 係車費；non-money cost 係佢時間嘅最佳其他用途，即係邊樣？
explain_en: Money cost $20 + non-money cost $150 (best alternative use of time: fishing) = $170.
explain_zh: Money cost $20 + non-money cost $150（時間最佳其他用途：打魚）= $170。

prompt_en: If factory pay rises to $220, Grandpa's opportunity cost of drying salt rises.
prompt_zh: 工廠人工升到 $220，阿爺繼續曬鹽嘅 opportunity cost 會上升。
hint_en: Is the factory the highest-valued option forgone?
hint_zh: 工廠係咪被放棄嘅最高價值選項？
explain_en: The highest-valued option forgone became more valuable, so opportunity cost rises.
explain_zh: 被放棄嘅最高價值選項價值上升，opportunity cost 上升。

prompt_en: Grandpa wants to borrow to buy a motorised boat. If the interest rate rises, his willingness to borrow will:
prompt_zh: 阿爺想借錢買機動船出海。利率上升，佢借錢嘅意願會：
options_zh: 下降|上升|不變|無法判斷
hint_en: Does the cost of earlier availability rise or fall?
hint_zh: 提早得到資源嘅成本變高定變低？
explain_en: Higher interest rate → higher cost of earlier availability → lower willingness to borrow.
explain_zh: 利率上升 → 提早得到資源嘅成本上升 → 借錢意願下降。

prompt_en: Last question: free good or economic good?
prompt_zh: 最後一題：free good 定 economic good？
options_zh: 免費物品|經濟物品
items_en: seawater in the ocean|sun-dried salt|sunlight|salted fish
items_zh: 大海嘅海水|曬好嘅鹽|陽光|鹹魚
hint_en: Is the quantity enough for everyone?
hint_zh: 數量夠唔夠滿足所有人？
explain_en: Seawater and sunlight are sufficient; salt and salted fish need scarce resources.
explain_zh: 海水同陽光數量夠晒；鹽同鹹魚要用 scarce resources 生產。

prompt_en: Which basic economic problem does each villager proposal belong to?
prompt_zh: 村民嘅提議屬於邊個基本經濟問題？
options_zh: 生產咩|點生產|為誰生產
items_en: switch to vegetables or oysters|by hand or by machine|share the catch by highest bid or by seniority
items_zh: 改種菜定養蠔|用人手定用機器|漁獲按價高者得定按輩份分
hint_en: What, how, or for whom?
hint_zh: 揀緊生產咩、點生產，定係俾邊個？
explain_en: The three problems: what, how, for whom.
explain_zh: 三個問題：生產咩、點生產、俾邊個。

prompt_en: Cheaper imported salt made Tai O's salt industry decline. This reflects which method?
prompt_zh: 入口鹽較平，令大澳鹽業式微，反映邊種解決方法？
options_zh: 市場機制|政府指令|習俗與傳統|以物易物
hint_en: Did anyone order salt workers to stop?
hint_zh: 有冇人下命令叫鹽工停手？
explain_en: Price signals moved resources away; no one gave orders.
explain_zh: 價格訊號令資源流走，冇人下令。

prompt_en: Put in order:
prompt_zh: 排出次序：
items_en: private property rights|exchange|specialisation
items_zh: 私有產權|交換|專門化
hint_en: Which makes which possible?
hint_zh: 邊個令邊個成為可能？
explain_en: Clear ownership → confident exchange → confident specialisation.
explain_zh: 業權清楚 → 放心交換 → 放心專門化。

prompt_en: Complete the circular flow:
prompt_zh: 完成 circular flow 圖：
options_zh: 住戶→廠商（生產要素市場）|廠商→住戶（生產要素市場）|廠商→住戶（產品市場）|住戶→廠商（產品市場）
items_en: factor services|factor income|goods and services|households' expenditure
items_zh: 生產要素服務|要素收入|物品與服務|住戶支出
hint_en: Each market: one real flow, one money flow.
hint_zh: 每個市場一條實物、一條錢。
explain_en: Each market has a real flow and a money flow going in opposite directions.
explain_zh: 每個市場都有一條 real flow 同一條 money flow，方向相反。

prompt_en: Villagers' remarks: positive or normative?
prompt_zh: 村民講嘅說話：positive 定 normative？
options_zh: 實證性|規範性
items_en: A road into Tai O was built in 1969–1970|Salt workers should get subsidies|Tai O's population began falling in the 1970s|Stilt houses are the most beautiful buildings|Imported salt is cheaper than local salt
items_zh: 1969–1970 年大澳要起公路|鹽工應該有補助|大澳人口喺 1970 年代開始下降|棚屋係最靚嘅建築|入口鹽比本地鹽平
hint_en: Can facts refute it?
hint_zh: 可唔可以用事實推翻？
explain_en: Positive can be refuted by facts; normative is a value judgement.
explain_zh: Positive 可以用事實推翻；normative 係價值判斷。

prompt_en: With fewer yellow croakers, the fish stall switches to first come first served. This is:
prompt_zh: 黃花魚少咗，魚檔改做排隊先到先得，屬於：
options_zh: 非價格競爭|價格競爭|政府指令|交換
hint_en: Is price the criterion?
hint_zh: 準則係價格嗎？
explain_en: The criterion is order of arrival, not price.
explain_zh: 準則係時間先後，唔係價格。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Grandpa keeps drying salt ($120/month). He gave up factory work ($180/month, $20 monthly fares) and fishing ($150/month). As Tai O's yellow croaker catch fell, fishing income drops to $100. Explain whether his opportunity cost of drying salt changes. (3 marks)
prompt_zh: （虛構）阿爺繼續曬鹽（每月 $120），放棄咗工廠打工（每月 $180，車費每月 $20）同打魚（每月 $150）。大澳黃花魚漁獲下跌，打魚收入跌到 $100。解釋阿爺曬鹽嘅 opportunity cost 會唔會改變。（3 分）
options_en: Opportunity cost is the value of the highest-valued option forgone when a choice is made.|Even after the $20 fares, factory work is still the highest-valued option forgone, worth more than fishing at $150 or $100.|So the fall in fishing income does not change his opportunity cost of drying salt, which is still the value of factory work.|His opportunity cost falls from $330 to $280, because both forgone options must be added together.|His opportunity cost falls, because one of the options he gave up has become less valuable.|His opportunity cost is $120, the income he earns from drying salt.|Fishing is his opportunity cost because, unlike factory work, it needs no fares.
options_zh: Opportunity cost 係作出選擇時，被放棄嘅最高價值選項嘅價值。|就算扣埋 $20 車費，工廠打工仍然係被放棄嘅最高價值選項，高過打魚嘅 $150 或 $100。|所以打魚收入下跌唔會改變佢曬鹽嘅 opportunity cost，仍然係工廠打工嘅價值。|佢嘅 opportunity cost 由 $330 跌到 $280，因為兩個被放棄嘅選項要加埋一齊計。|佢嘅 opportunity cost 下降，因為其中一個被放棄嘅選項價值下跌咗。|佢嘅 opportunity cost 係 $120，即係曬鹽賺到嘅收入。|打魚先係佢嘅 opportunity cost，因為唔似工廠打工，打魚唔使俾車費。
hint_en: Which option forgone is worth the most, before and after the change?
hint_zh: 改變之前同之後，被放棄嘅選項之中邊個價值最高？
explain_en: 1 mark for the definition (highest-valued option forgone only), 1 mark for applying it (factory work is still highest), 1 mark for the conclusion (no change). Adding options together is a classic error.
explain_zh: 定義 1 分（只計最高價值嘅放棄選項）、應用 1 分（工廠打工仍然最高）、結論 1 分（唔變）。將選項加埋一齊係典型錯誤。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Grandpa decides to take the factory job ($180/month, $20 monthly fares). His other options were drying salt ($120) and fishing ($150). Calculate and explain the full cost of taking the factory job. (4 marks)
prompt_zh: （虛構）阿爺決定出市區工廠打工（每月 $180，車費每月 $20）。佢其他選擇係曬鹽（$120）同打魚（$150）。計算並解釋揀工廠打工嘅 full cost。（4 分）
options_en: Full cost is money cost plus non-money cost.|The money cost is the $20 monthly fare he pays to get to the factory.|The non-money cost is the best alternative use of his time: fishing at $150, which is higher than salt at $120.|So the full cost of taking the factory job is $20 + $150 = $170 per month.|The non-money cost is $270, the income from salt and fishing added together.|The full cost is $200, the factory wage plus the fares.|The fare is not a cost, because the factory wage is high enough to cover it.
options_zh: Full cost = money cost + non-money cost。|Money cost 係佢每月返工要俾嘅 $20 車費。|Non-money cost 係佢時間嘅最佳其他用途：打魚 $150，高過曬鹽 $120。|所以揀工廠打工嘅 full cost 係 $20 + $150 = 每月 $170。|Non-money cost 係 $270，即係曬鹽同打魚收入加埋。|Full cost 係 $200，即係工廠人工加車費。|車費唔算 cost，因為工廠人工夠高，抵銷得到。
hint_en: What does Grandpa pay in money, and what is the best thing he could have done with that time?
hint_zh: 阿爺要俾咩錢？嗰段時間佢最好可以用嚟做咩？
explain_en: Marks: formula, money cost ($20), non-money cost = best alternative use of time ($150, not $120 or $270), and the $170 total. The factory wage is the benefit of the choice, not its cost.
explain_zh: 評分：公式、money cost（$20）、non-money cost = 時間最佳其他用途（$150，唔係 $120 或 $270），同埋總數 $170。工廠人工係選擇嘅得益，唔係 cost。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Last month Grandpa paid $80 for new salt rakes, which cannot be resold. Now he is thinking of switching to fishing. His grandson says: 'Switching would waste the $80, so keep drying salt.' Explain whether the grandson is correct. (2 marks)
prompt_zh: （虛構）上個月阿爺用 $80 買咗新鹽耙，呢啲鹽耙賣唔返出去。而家佢諗緊轉去打魚。個孫話：「轉行就嘥咗嗰 $80，所以繼續曬鹽啦。」解釋個孫講得啱唔啱。（2 分）
options_en: The $80 is a historical cost: it was spent in the past and cannot be recovered whatever Grandpa chooses now.|With no choice involved, there is no cost, so the $80 should not affect his decision and the grandson is incorrect.|The $80 should be added to the cost of switching to fishing.|The $80 should be added to the cost of continuing to dry salt.|The $80 is the opportunity cost of continuing to dry salt.|The grandson is correct, because wasting resources always raises the cost of a choice.|Even if the rakes could be resold for $50, that $50 would still be a historical cost.
options_zh: 嗰 $80 係 historical cost：已經喺過去用咗，而家阿爺點揀都拎唔返。|冇選擇就冇 cost，所以 $80 唔應該影響佢嘅決定，個孫講得唔啱。|嗰 $80 應該加入轉去打魚嘅 cost 度。|嗰 $80 應該加入繼續曬鹽嘅 cost 度。|嗰 $80 係繼續曬鹽嘅 opportunity cost。|個孫講得啱，因為嘥資源一定會令選擇嘅 cost 上升。|就算鹽耙可以賣返 $50，嗰 $50 都仍然係 historical cost。
hint_en: Can the $80 be recovered whichever option Grandpa picks today?
hint_zh: 無論阿爺今日揀邊樣，嗰 $80 拎唔拎得返？
explain_en: 1 mark for identifying historical cost (spent and unrecoverable), 1 mark for 'no choice, no cost' leading to the conclusion. A resale value would be recoverable, so it would be an opportunity cost, not a historical cost.
explain_zh: 指出 historical cost（已用咗、拎唔返）1 分；「冇選擇就冇 cost」並得出結論 1 分。如果可以轉賣，轉賣價值拎得返，就係 opportunity cost，唔係 historical cost。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Grandpa borrows $1,000 from Uncle Wing to buy a motorised fishing boat now, and repays $1,100 one year later. Explain what the $100 interest means to each of them. (3 marks)
prompt_zh: （虛構）阿爺向榮叔借 $1,000，即刻買一隻機動漁船，一年後還 $1,100。解釋呢 $100 interest 對佢哋兩個分別有咩意思。（3 分）
options_en: For Grandpa, the borrower, interest is the cost of earlier availability: he gets the boat now instead of after saving up.|For Uncle Wing, the lender, interest is the compensation for postponing his consumption of $1,000 for a year.|The interest rate is $100 / $1,000 = 10% per year.|For Grandpa, interest is the compensation for postponing his consumption.|For Uncle Wing, interest is the cost of earlier availability of the boat.|The interest rate is 11%, because Grandpa repays $1,100.|Once the loan is signed, the $100 interest is a historical cost to Grandpa.
options_zh: 對借款人阿爺嚟講，interest 係提早得到資源嘅 cost：佢而家就有船，唔使儲夠錢先買。|對貸款人榮叔嚟講，interest 係佢延遲一年使用嗰 $1,000 嘅補償。|Interest rate 係 $100 / $1,000 = 每年 10%。|對阿爺嚟講，interest 係延遲消費嘅補償。|對榮叔嚟講，interest 係提早得到漁船嘅 cost。|Interest rate 係 11%，因為阿爺要還 $1,100。|一簽咗借據，嗰 $100 interest 對阿爺嚟講就係 historical cost。
hint_en: Who enjoys the resources earlier, and who waits?
hint_zh: 邊個提早享用資源？邊個要等？
explain_en: Borrower: cost of earlier availability. Lender: compensation for postponing consumption. Rate = interest / principal. Swapping the two roles is the common mistake.
explain_zh: 借款人：提早得到資源嘅 cost。貸款人：延遲消費嘅補償。利率 = interest / 本金。調轉兩個角色係常見錯誤。

prompt_en: (Fictional) After WWII, cheaper imported salt competed with Tai O salt. Salt pan owners turned their pans into fish ponds without any government order. Explain which basic economic problem this solves and how. (3 marks)
prompt_zh: （虛構）二戰後，平價入口鹽同大澳鹽競爭。鹽田主喺冇政府命令之下，將鹽田改做魚塘。解釋呢件事解決緊邊個基本經濟問題，同埋點樣解決。（3 分）
options_en: It concerns the 'what to produce' problem: whether the land produces salt or fish.|It is solved by the market mechanism: cheaper imported salt lowered the price and profit of local salt, sending a signal.|Owners, as private property owners, voluntarily moved their resources to the more profitable use, fish ponds.|It concerns the 'how to produce' problem, because the land is now used in a different way.|It concerns the 'for whom' problem, because fish ponds decide who gets to eat fish.|It is solved by command, because the decline of the salt industry forced owners to change.|It is solved by tradition, because villagers follow what their ancestors did.
options_zh: 呢件事關於「生產咩」（what）問題：塊地用嚟生產鹽定魚。|佢由 market mechanism 解決：入口鹽較平，令本地鹽嘅價格同利潤下跌，發出訊號。|鹽田主作為私有產權擁有人，自願將資源轉去利潤較高嘅用途，即係魚塘。|呢件事關於「點生產」（how）問題，因為塊地而家用法唔同咗。|呢件事關於「為誰生產」（for whom）問題，因為魚塘決定邊個有魚食。|佢由 command 解決，因為鹽業式微迫使鹽田主轉變。|佢由 tradition 解決，因為村民跟返祖先嘅做法。
hint_en: Is the decision about which good, which method, or who gets it? Who gave the signal?
hint_zh: 個決定係關於生產邊樣、用咩方法，定俾邊個？邊個發出訊號？
explain_en: 1 mark for the correct problem (what), 1 mark for price as the signal, 1 mark for owners responding voluntarily. Being 'forced' by prices is not command, which requires government orders.
explain_zh: 指出正確問題（what）1 分、價格做訊號 1 分、業主自願回應 1 分。俾價格「迫」唔等於 command，command 要有政府命令。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Ah Kei owns a fishing boat and Ah Lan owns a shrimp paste workshop, both with clear ownership. Explain how private property rights enable them to specialise. (3 marks)
prompt_zh: （虛構）阿琦擁有一隻漁船，阿蘭擁有一間蝦醬工場，兩個業權都清清楚楚。解釋 private property rights 點樣令佢哋可以 specialise。（3 分）
options_en: Private property rights give owners the exclusive right to use, to receive income from, and to transfer their resources.|With clear ownership, Ah Kei can confidently exchange his shrimps for Ah Lan's shrimp paste or money, without fear of seizure.|Since they can rely on exchange, each specialises in one job, fishing or making shrimp paste, and trades for the rest.|Specialisation comes first; private property rights appear only after people have specialised.|Private property rights mean the government decides who may use the boat and the workshop.|Exchange only happens when money is used, so bartering shrimps for shrimp paste is not exchange.|Private property rights let owners use their property in any way, even if it harms others.
options_zh: Private property rights 俾擁有人專有使用權、專有收益權同轉讓權。|業權清楚，阿琦可以放心用佢嘅銀蝦同阿蘭交換蝦醬或者錢，唔怕俾人搶。|因為可以靠交換，佢哋各自專門做一樣嘢，打魚或者整蝦醬，其餘嘅靠交換得到。|先有 specialisation，大家專門化咗之後先出現 private property rights。|Private property rights 即係由政府決定邊個可以用隻船同間工場。|用錢先算交換，所以用銀蝦換蝦醬唔算 exchange。|Private property rights 令擁有人可以任意使用財產，就算傷害到其他人都得。
hint_en: What would happen to trade if anyone could take Ah Kei's catch?
hint_zh: 如果人人都可以攞走阿琦嘅漁獲，交易會點？
explain_en: The chain is: private property rights (1 mark) → confident exchange (1 mark) → specialisation (1 mark). Barter is also exchange, and property rights are not unlimited.
explain_zh: 因果鏈：private property rights（1 分）→ 放心 exchange（1 分）→ specialisation（1 分）。以物易物都係 exchange，而產權唔係冇限制。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Only 30 kg of yellow croaker reach Hoi Tse's stall, but buyers want 50 kg. She can either raise the price or sell to regular customers first. Explain why competition implies discrimination here and classify each method. (4 marks)
prompt_zh: （虛構）海姐個檔只得 30 kg 黃花魚，但買家想要 50 kg。佢可以加價，或者先賣俾熟客。解釋點解呢度 competition 意味住 discrimination，並將兩個方法分類。（4 分）
options_en: Yellow croaker is scarce: the quantity is not enough for all buyers, so they must compete for it.|Competition implies discrimination: some criterion must be used to decide who gets the fish and who does not.|Raising the price is price competition: the buyers who are willing to pay the most get the fish.|Selling to regular customers first is non-price competition: the criterion is the relationship, not the price paid.|Selling to regular customers first is price competition, because they still pay for the fish.|Discrimination only happens when the criterion is unfair, such as a buyer's race.|If Hoi Tse does not raise the price, there is no competition among buyers.
options_zh: 黃花魚係 scarce：數量唔夠滿足所有買家，所以佢哋要競爭。|Competition 意味住 discrimination：一定要用某個準則決定邊個有魚、邊個冇。|加價係 price competition：願意俾最多錢嘅買家得到條魚。|先賣俾熟客係 non-price competition：準則係關係，唔係俾幾多錢。|先賣俾熟客都係 price competition，因為佢哋一樣要俾錢買魚。|要準則唔公平，例如睇買家種族，先算 discrimination。|如果海姐唔加價，買家之間就冇 competition。
hint_en: With not enough fish for everyone, how is the winner chosen in each method?
hint_zh: 條魚唔夠分，兩個方法分別用咩準則揀邊個得到？
explain_en: Scarcity → competition (1), competition → discrimination by a criterion (1), price as criterion = price competition (1), any other criterion = non-price competition (1). In economics, discrimination is neutral, not necessarily unfair.
explain_zh: Scarcity → competition（1 分）；competition → 用準則 discrimination（1 分）；以價格做準則 = price competition（1 分）；其他準則 = non-price competition（1 分）。經濟學嘅 discrimination 係中性，唔一定唔公平。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Ah Sang works in a Tai O shrimp paste factory for $150 a month and spends $30 buying shrimp paste from it. Explain these four flows using the circular flow model. (4 marks)
prompt_zh: （虛構）阿生喺大澳一間蝦醬廠打工，每月人工 $150，又用 $30 向間廠買蝦醬。用 circular flow 模型解釋呢四條流向。（4 分）
options_en: Ah Sang's labour is a real flow of factor services from households to firms in the factor market.|His $150 wage is a money flow of factor income from firms to households in the factor market.|The shrimp paste is a real flow of goods from firms to households in the product market.|His $30 is a money flow of household expenditure from households to firms in the product market.|His wage is paid in the product market, because it comes from the factory's shrimp paste sales.|His labour is a money flow, because he is paid money for it.|The shrimp paste and the $30 flow in the same direction, as both go through the product market.
options_zh: 阿生嘅勞力係 real flow：factor services 喺 factor market 由 households 流去 firms。|佢嘅 $150 人工係 money flow：factor income 喺 factor market 由 firms 流去 households。|蝦醬係 real flow：物品喺 product market 由 firms 流去 households。|佢嘅 $30 係 money flow：household expenditure 喺 product market 由 households 流去 firms。|佢嘅人工喺 product market 支付，因為錢嚟自間廠賣蝦醬嘅收入。|佢嘅勞力係 money flow，因為佢做嘢有錢收。|蝦醬同 $30 流向一樣，因為兩樣都經過 product market。
hint_en: For each flow: real or money? Which market? Which direction?
hint_zh: 每條流向：real 定 money？邊個市場？咩方向？
explain_en: 1 mark per flow, each needing real or money, the correct market and the correct direction. In each market the real flow and the money flow go in opposite directions.
explain_zh: 每條流向 1 分，要講啱 real 定 money、邊個市場同方向。每個市場入面，real flow 同 money flow 方向相反。
